title: Characterizing Local Breadth in Language Generation
summary: In the Kleinberg–Mullainathan generation-in-the-limit model, measures breadth by lower Banach density and characterises the optimal achievable breadth exactly in 1-D; in d≥2 there is no single best generator, and the full region of achievable density profiles is characterised.

title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
summary: Shows the two natural sequence-level losses that bake greedy decoding or sampling into training are unbounded below, links them via autoregressive Gumbel tricks, and proves the stop-gradient 'moment matching' direction is a valid descent direction for NLL in function space — but too noisy, so teacher forcing stays.

title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
summary: Treats an SSM's state update as a linear representation of the input monoid: an SSM tracks a group exactly when the group is a quotient of the group its transition matrices generate, so diagonal real/complex SSMs track only commutative groups; quaternion blocks (HyperSSM) fix S5 tracking.

title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
summary: Estimates all leave-one-out context-attribution values of an n-token prompt with O(√log(1/ε)/ε) model calls under a stability assumption, with a matching lower bound, via sketching arithmetic circuits with decaying Taylor coefficients.

title: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
summary: Early termination for (constrained) k-NN on graph indexes with a guarantee that the answer is exact with probability ≥1−ε; risk-constrained stopping becomes an LP over an order polytope whose Lagrangian minimisers are staircase rules computed by DP, then calibrated with fixed-sequence binomial tests, plus a lower bound on the optimum of the rule family.

title: Two mathematical models of knowledge distillation
summary: Two analysable models of knowledge distillation (GLMs under SGD; rank-1 matrix approximation) showing distillation helps by making optimisation faster, not by generalising better.

title: When and How SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Functional Scaling Law Perspective
summary: Functional scaling law for SignSGD in power-law kernel regression: gradient noise smooths the sign, acting as a preconditioner that maps H to H^{1/2}; faster signal learning, slower noise forgetting, giving regime-dependent advantages over SGD.

title: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms
summary: Binary tokenization (choose ≤K substrings minimising token count) has no polynomial n^{1−ε}-approximation unless P=NP; gives (γ,γ)-bicriteria algorithms with γ=√M log n, and a storage-budget variant.

title: Finding the Farthest in High Dimensions: Dynamic Diameter and Farthest-Neighbor Search
summary: Dynamic c-approximate diameter and farthest-neighbour search in high dimensions with better update/space exponents than Indyk (SODA'03), robust to adaptive updates.

title: From Link Prediction to Linear Community Detection: A Finite-Sample Guarantee for Graph Pretraining
summary: In a finite-sample SBM, small held-out link-prediction risk with a bilinear decoder implies small error for linear community classification on the learned embeddings, with explicit Õ(√(d/n)) terms.

title: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries
summary: Characterises all parameter symmetries of (leaky) ReLU nets (positive channel scaling and permutation) and turns them into sharp covering-number bounds: exponent S−H and a G! divisor, with matching lower bounds.

title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate
summary: Formulates learning from a debate-judging human as online learning; shows adversarial debate is not always the best way to learn, and characterises a cooperative protocol's learnability by a combinatorial dimension.

title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
summary: Closes the gap for online smooth calibration: a new adversary forces Ω(√T) error, matching the known upper bound.

title: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous
summary: Shows that with same-state positive pairs the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis becomes vacuous (every whitened state function is a minimiser); one of four quantitative results survives.

title: Trait Hitchhiking in LLM Post-Training
summary: Models how RL post-training amplifies or suppresses untargeted 'traits' using the Price equation from evolutionary biology; the Price estimate tracks trait dynamics under GRPO.

title: Pretraining Data Statistics Shape the Phases of Learning Entity Comparison in Language Models
summary: Small LMs learn entity comparison in three data-determined phases — pick by frequency, then by position, then correctly; Zipfian vs uniform entity frequency changes the phases.

title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
summary: Apparent compositional generalization of transformers mostly exploits 'composition equivalences' (different module sequences, same function); removing them collapses performance.

title: When Direction Matters: Diagnosing Relational Instruction Following in Dense Retrieval
summary: SwitchIR: dense and late-interaction retrievers follow lexical/attribute instructions but fail when only the direction of a relation flips; an exact margin decomposition locates the failure.

title: Search-by-Answer Bias in Retrieval Models
summary: Dense retrievers favour passages containing answers their backbone LM already knows, even over passages that state the answer — a 'search-by-answer' bias.

title: ReSID: Rethinking Long-Tail Retrieval in Generative Recommendation through Item Reachability
summary: Long-tail reachability in generative recommendation: parallel SIDs beat sequential ones on tail items; beam search pruning bounds recovery.

title: RoutingTrie: Metadata Routing for Constrained Generative Retrieval
summary: Shopify: metadata constraints applied before beam selection in generative retrieval.

title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation
summary: Semantic IDs as tree paths with an adaptive branching factor per node.

title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
summary: Alibaba generative ad retrieval for delivery search.

title: RecoGEM: A Serving System for Production-Scale Generative Recommendation
summary: Production serving system for generative recommendation.

title: From Tokens to Behaviors: Rethinking Generative Recommendation for User Trajectory Prediction
summary: Predicts a user's future behaviour sequence rather than only the next item.

title: TriGen: A Generative Paradigm for Trigger-Induced Recommendation
summary: Alibaba generative recommender for trigger-induced (click-opened) feeds.

title: SepLRM: A Foundation Model Paradigm for Recommendation
summary: ByteDance splits large rec models into a shared long-history encoder and light task models.

title: REWEAVE: Online Learning for Workload-Adaptive HNSW Indexes
summary: Online rewiring of HNSW edges for skewed or shifting query workloads under the same degree cap.

title: HyperPage: Learned Page Layouts for Disk-Resident Graph Vector Indexes
summary: Learned page layouts for disk-resident graph indexes (DiskANN-style) from traversal logs.

title: Authenticated Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in Outsourced Vector Databases
summary: Authenticated graph-based ANN for outsourced vector DBs using vector commitments.

title: VecDBLens: An Evaluatology-Based Framework for Vector Database Diagnosis
summary: Framework attributing vector-DB performance to embedding, index or query execution.

title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
summary: Meta's mini-batch k-means variant with moving-average updates and scaling-law hyperparameters.

title: AntEmbed: Dual-Mode Multimodal Embedding Model for Efficient and Fine-Grained Retrieval
summary: Ant Group multimodal embedding model with fast and reasoning-enhanced modes.

title: Yuanbao-Reranker: Document-Grounded Synthesis and Preference Distillation for Text Reranking
summary: 0.6B/4B/8B text rerankers trained on document-grounded synthetic data.

title: MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface
summary: Meta compares scoring designs for bi-encoders in decision-making with a natural-language interface.

title: Beyond Ranking: Are Decision Models Calibrated Relevance Scorers?
summary: Relevance probabilities from LLM decision models are not calibrated to human judgments.

title: Process then Retrieve: Investigating the Origins of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
summary: Traces the VLM modality gap to vision tokens being much more semantically dense than text tokens.

title: Exploiting Feature-invariant Scaling Laws for Efficient A/B Experimentation in Recommendation Systems
summary: Meta predicts full-scale A/B results for rec models from feature-invariant scaling laws.

title: Calibrating Document-Local Boundaries for Contextual Chunk Retrieval
summary: Improves late-chunking retrieval by separating the right chunk from similar ones in the same document.

title: Hybrid Product Search Without the Copy: Lexical, Semantic and Filtered Retrieval Served Directly from a Data Lake
summary: BM25 + semantic + filtered retrieval served directly from a data lake (Apache Pinot).

title: Proactive Dimension-Adaptive Denoising for Graph Collaborative Filtering via Representation Coherence
summary: Denoising graph CF by flagging interactions that deviate from a user's representation coherence.

title: Sheaf-Inspired Structured Scoring Extensions of LightGCN for Collaborative Filtering
summary: Sheaf-inspired scoring extensions of LightGCN.

title: KuaiRecV2: Benchmarking Large-Scale Continual Learning for Diversified and Multi-task Recommendation
summary: Kuaishou benchmark for large-scale continual multi-task recommendation.

title: TRIAD: Multimodal Retrieval across Abstraction, Constraints, and State
summary: Multimodal retrieval benchmark over concept hierarchies, joint constraints and state.

title: DocFS: File Systems as Agentic Reasoning Environments for Complex Multimodal Document Question Answering
summary: Documents turned into file systems as an agentic environment for multimodal document QA.

title: CURATOR: Scalable Fine-grained Evidence Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Decision Models
summary: Amazon fine-tunes a decision model to select fine-grained evidence for RAG.

title: From Search to Decision: How Post-Training Shapes Information-Seeking Capabilities in Large Language Models
summary: Survey of how post-training teaches LLMs when and how to search.

title: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication
summary: RMIT at TREC RAG 2026: research agents, retriever ablations, open-weight replication.

title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
summary: Studies task orchestration/delegation in generative search systems.

title: Active Learning of Approximate LLM Ranking for Energy-Efficient Retrieval of Long Queries
summary: Active learning of an approximate LLM ranker for energy-efficient retrieval of long queries.

title: SurvEval: Listwise Re-Ranking Evaluator via Survival-Based Exposure and Multi-Objective Value Modeling
summary: Listwise re-ranking evaluator built on survival-based exposure modelling.

title: ReAlign: Reward-Guided Preference Alignment for Generative Re-Ranking
summary: Reward-guided preference alignment for generative re-ranking.

title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
summary: Learning to search, ask and recommend from simulated interaction.

title: When Does a Recommendation Spark Curiosity? Theory, Measurement, and Field Evidence
summary: Axiomatises the information-gap theory of curiosity into a computable measure for recommendation, validated in a survey and field data.

title: Characterizing Predictive Multiplicity in Ranking and Its Fairness Implications
summary: Formal definitions and guarantees for predictive multiplicity in score-based ranking.

title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
summary: With the right data mix and matched rollout budget, SFT generalises as well as or better than RL.

title: Rectified Looped Transformer
summary: Interpolation between loops keeps hidden-state norms bounded in looped transformers; lower perplexity.

title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
summary: A learned Hopfield–Tank energy solves Sudoku-Extreme/Maze ~1000× faster than looped models — a caution about these benchmarks.

title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
summary: Unbundling multimodal vision encoding.

title: Measuring, Revealing and Mitigating Harmful Content Propagation in Recommender Systems
summary: Measuring and mitigating harmful-content propagation in recommender systems (TPAMI).

title: Unraveling Syntax: Language Modeling and the Substructure of Grammars
summary: Defines subgrammars of a context-free grammar and proves that the language-modeling loss recurses linearly over top-level subgrammars, so it decomposes into losses on irreducible subgrammars. Under further assumptions (and empirically) models learn subgrammars in parallel rather than simple-first; subgrammar pretraining only helps tiny models but makes internal representations align better with the grammar's structure.

title: Finding the Minimal Parameter Budget for Implicit Reasoning: A Data Complexity Driven Scaling Law for Language Models
summary: Pretrains LMs from scratch on synthetic knowledge graphs and measures the smallest model that can infer held-out edges by implicit multi-hop reasoning. The optimal parameter budget follows a scaling law in a graph search-entropy measure; an optimally sized model handles at most about 0.008 bits of reasoning information per parameter.

title: Progressive Cramming: Reliable Token Compression and What It Reveals
summary: Grows the prefix crammed into a single learned input embedding token by token until reconstruction fails, to separate optimisation failures from capacity limits. Cramming trajectories lie in low-dimensional structure; prepending a crammed embedding degrades downstream generation sharply, traced to early-layer interactions, so perfect reconstruction works by brittle steering rather than transferable semantics.

title: Dimensional Collapse in Transformer Attention Outputs: A Challenge for Sparse Dictionary Learning
summary: Attention outputs across model families occupy a subspace of only about 60% of the hidden dimension, caused by overlap among heads' output subspaces. This low rank explains most dead features in attention-output SAEs; initialising SAE features inside the active subspace cuts dead features from 87% to under 1%.

title: Provable Cross-Modal Transfer of Hierarchical Concept Structure in CLIP Embeddings
summary: Defines Hierarchical Angular Separation (a parent concept embedding is closer to its descendants than to off-branch concepts) and analyses an unconstrained-features model with fixed image embeddings and trained text embeddings. At the global minimizer, text-side HAS violations are bounded by image-side violations; the driver is the hierarchical co-occurrence of image-text pairs, which pulls text embeddings toward root-centred image prototypes. Closed form for a linear contrastive loss, analogous guarantees for InfoNCE with enough regularization.

title: Classification with Large-Step Gradient Descent: Unifying Self-Stabilization and Convergence Rates
summary: Extends the self-stabilization view of large-step GD from least squares to separable linear classification with logistic and multiclass cross-entropy, where no finite minimizer exists. A curvature-defined reference subspace replaces the minimizer manifold, giving iterate bounds in both unstable and stable regimes (three-phase damping). Large steps leave orthogonal residuals that can delay alignment with the max-margin direction.

title: Offline KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Stochastic Transitions
summary: Sample complexity of offline KL-regularized RL in finite discounted MDPs with stochastic transitions: a lower bound Omega(KCH^3/(eps*max(eps,beta))) under concentrability C, matched by pessimistic soft value iteration when beta >= 1.4H. Data from the reference policy itself cover the regularized optimum up to a power law in H/beta, so no coverage assumption is needed; the plug-in estimator can fail at small temperature.

title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining
summary: In Muon-trained decoder-only transformers (162M to 3.4B), a temporary weight-decay window can raise validation loss when removed yet lower final loss; moving the window from early to late reverses its effect. The mechanism is a persistent weight-norm deficit that keeps relative step sizes larger, captured by an approximate norm-dynamics recurrence and fixed-norm replays.

title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations
summary: Measures per-layer autocorrelation of activations across context positions; slowly decaying tails grow with depth. In synthetic data with hierarchical latent structure this comes from encoding persistent abstract latents; in LLMs, SAE-feature persistence time grows with depth and tracks the autocorrelation, and ablating persistent features lowers it.

title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
summary: When does sharing MoE experts across steps help the final output, not just local error? In linear regression models it derives exact sharing/merging criteria (variance saved vs bias across roles) and builds cases where sharing lowers local error but raises final-output error; gives end-to-end bounds for routed computations and shows correct routes do not certify that an expert implements the attributed operation.

title: Adversarially Batched Online Learning
summary: Online learning where the learner may only update at adversarially chosen batch boundaries. For OCO, experts and adversarial bandits the optimal regret is characterized by the 2-norm of the batch-length sequence, achieved by a batch-oblivious adaptive doubling trick; stochastic bandits get a relative-batch-growth complexity measure with gap-dependent and gap-independent bounds.

title: Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity under Shuffling
summary: Muon with polar-map orthogonalization under any shuffling scheme reaches an eps-stationary point in O(eps^-3) iterations on smooth nonconvex finite sums, matching shuffled SGD and improving on O(eps^-4) with replacement, provided beta tends to 1 with the number of components. For any fixed beta there are smooth convex problems where Muon stays away from stationarity.

title: Analyzing Learning-Dynamics Across Loss and Prediction Choices for Diffusion Models
summary: For denoisers, changing the loss space at fixed prediction target is exactly a timestep reweighting. A rank-m linear bottleneck on a D-dimensional input forces an irreducible error floor D-m for noise and velocity prediction, while x-prediction can exploit low-dimensional data; experiments on U-Net/JiT match the bound.

title: The Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective
summary: The authors of the 2016 PL-condition paper look back after its ECML-PKDD test-of-time award: origins, a refined main theorem, criticisms, and extensions.

title: Neural Classifiers as Error-Correcting Codes
summary: Frames softmax classification as maximum-likelihood decoding of an error-correcting code: cross-entropy aligns logits with Hamming distances to learned class codewords, and neural-collapse geometry is an optimal constellation under isotropic noise. Derives criteria for lossless quantization and distillation from code redundancy.

title: Contrastive latent representation learning with denoising score matching
summary: ScoreCLR replaces the explicit negatives in contrastive learning with a learned repulsion: the entropy gradient is written via the score of the latent distribution, estimated by denoising score matching with a small network. Cost linear in batch size; near-SimCLR linear-probe accuracy with higher effective rank.

title: Tight Bounds for k-Median++ and Improved Bounds for k-Means++
summary: Tight analysis of k-means++ / D^l sampling: exact ratio 2(1+H_{k-1}) for k-median, (1+phi)(1+H_{k-1}) for Euclidean k-means (was 5), and sharper bi-criteria bounds (10% extra centres gives 5.7).

title: Small Is Not Dead: Distance-Aware Cluster Revival for e-means
summary: Adds a centre-distance condition to the dead-cluster revival of e-means (mini-batch k-means in FAISS), so small but isolated clusters are not removed; identical on the original embedding benchmarks, 10-80% lower error on data with rare isolated groups.

title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
summary: Learned pair-specific weighted Euclidean distance approximating DTW for time-series similarity search, used as a filter before exact DTW verification; 11x faster than the fastest exact method at recall@10 0.93. Notes that regression to DTW distances alone misorders nearest neighbours without a ranking regularizer.

title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
summary: Incremental visual embedding for screenshot streams (token pruning plus KV reuse for unchanged blocks) with a benchmark of 10k questions over 184 hours of screen history; up to 3.7x faster encoding than full screenshots at equal accuracy.

title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
summary: Compresses long user histories for generative recommendation into a fixed set of memory slots with forget-gated updates; keeps 87.9% of HSTU-1200's Recall@10 with a 216-token context, with a horizon-independent bound on the discrepancy between sequential and packed processing.

title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
summary: Instance-adaptive compression for sequential recommenders: a list-wise ranking-uncertainty score predicted from early layers decides per-instance channel and sequence pruning.

title: Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders
summary: Sparse autoencoders on dense text embeddings for medical retrieval, trained with reconstruction plus InfoNCE; sparse codes improve in-domain retrieval and lose less out of domain than the dense embeddings.

title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging
summary: Learning an autoregressive next-token generator from a class F given length-T chain-of-thought demonstrations. A majority vote over O(log(T/delta)) CoT-consistent learners trained on bootstrap samples reaches the optimal O((d_VC + log(1/delta))/eps) sample complexity for binary tokens, independent of T; for finite alphabets the Graph dimension replaces VC, optimal up to log|Sigma|. The ensemble can be distilled into one generator in F using n log(nT) unlabeled prompts.

title: The Price of Choosing Examples: Context Overfitting in Adaptive In-Context Learning
summary: Treats prompt construction (retrieve, filter, re-rank, re-test) as adaptive data analysis. With context capacity kappa = mutual information (or max-information) between the data store and the final prompt, any frozen in-context learner obeys a context generalization bound of order sqrt(kappa/k) over k selected examples, with a matching lower bound. Gives PAC-Bayesian retrieval rules and an order-statistics analysis of query-aligned top-k Gaussian retrieval in Bayesian linear in-context regression.

title: The Price of Not Planning: Parallel Sampling Depth Peaks at the Reconstruction Threshold
summary: On broadcast trees (leaves = tokens, internal nodes = a plan, edge correlation theta), a masked diffusion decoder that samples each round independently needs order min{n,(n/eps)^alpha} rounds below the reconstruction threshold, alpha = log b / (4 log(1/theta)), rising to 1/2 at the threshold; with the plan, log_b n + 1 rounds suffice. A plan with units of m tokens gives logarithmic depth only when m is logarithmic. Lower bounds hold for any deterministic adaptive unmasking rule, including learned conditionals.

title: Understanding the Role of Reasoning Data in Pretraining
summary: Every fact gives an atomic training signal but only a subset appears in reasoning traces; the question is how much weight atomic facts should get. For a linear transformer the held-transition-optimal weight is derived in closed form to leading order: it grows with reasoning-chain length and shrinks with the fraction of facts held out of traces. The trends persist in a full softmax+MLP layer with cross-entropy and in controlled multi-hop and math pretraining experiments.

title: Conic Structure of the Cross-Entropy Loss at the Final Layer and Its Absence in Rectifier Backbones
summary: Over the weights of an affine final layer, softmax cross-entropy equals a polyhedral cone plus an offset that decays exponentially along every ray to a closed-form limit; the 'core radius' equals the mean surprisal of the favoured classes divided by the wall slope. Over ReLU backbone parameters, kinks along a line occur where one sample's activation pattern changes, and under a coprimality condition no large creases form.

title: Syntax vs. Semantics: How Transformers Learn Deep Dependencies
summary: Models learning as a competition between surface statistics and sparse deep dependencies; argues that error signals for the sparse dependencies are suppressed early ('gradient starvation'), so their learning appears as a sudden transition, and that CoT bypasses the suppression by externalizing intermediate steps. Checked from toy transformers to 7-8B models; proposes a topology-aligned contrastive objective for variable binding.

title: Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
summary: Minimizers of anisotropic exponential interaction energies on the sphere, the energy behind mean-field models of self-attention. For any SPD interaction matrix the minimizer has a smooth, strictly positive density (via an anisotropic Brownian motion and Feynman-Kac) and is the only fully supported stationary measure; gives a sampler and a Mathieu-series scheme in 2D.

title: Geometrically Disentangling Concept Learning from the Language Modeling Loss
summary: Concept Energy: alignment between a concept's probe subspace and the average gradient outer product (AGOP) of the next-token loss. Across 19 Pythia-410M/1B checkpoints and 12 concepts, the first Concept Energy peak comes at or before the steepest rise in probe accuracy, and some concepts show repeated engagement while probe accuracy only rises.

title: Attention Sinks as Spectral Spikes: A Mechanism Analysis of Gated Attention
summary: Formulates attention sinks as sink-induced low-rank spikes in token-space covariance aligned with high-mass attention columns. Post-SDPA output gating acts as a mode-dependent contraction: it reduces the sink spectral energy forward and the value-path gradients through sink columns backward; random-matrix diagnostics show lower outlier mass and higher effective rank.

title: A phase diagram for training and inference in language models
summary: Describes a document's representation at each layer by two coordinates, distinguishability and dimension, and tracks inference as a flow over depth. Untrained models flow into collapse or noise regions depending on initialization scale; 8 trained models from 5 families settle in a central region, which a discrete Langevin fit attributes to a stable-node rather than saddle effective force. Training of Pythia-1.4B reads as a phase transition.

title: Grokking Can Be Steered: Selecting Desirable Solutions By Choice Of Learning Rule
summary: On modular addition every grokking learning rule finds the same Fourier algorithm, but circuit size varies: a neuron stays in use when its credit is large relative to the non-gradient part of its update (weight decay, Adam's eps, gain decay). Per-neuron normalisation (Nero) spreads the computation to 99% of neurons; Adam, Muon, Shampoo and others keep small circuits, which prune and transfer better but tolerate deletion worse.

title: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization
summary: Mean pairwise cosine of mean-pooled encoder embeddings (e.g. DeBERTa-v3) mostly measures text length: truncating comments raises mean cosine by eight times a reported 'homogenization' effect, a length-matched placebo reproduces 78-81% of it, and one principal direction carries 99.9% of raw homogeneity. Proposes a diagnostic protocol.

title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data
summary: LeCat separates memorized category knowledge, generalization to unseen instances and context-dependent use. Pretraining-data analysis plus a 68M model trained from scratch with controlled data: verbatim rule-like repetition reduces flexible category learning, while diverse forms of expression and higher category-feature PMI improve it.

title: What Unlinked Aggregates Still Prove: Ranker Comparisons from Exact and Differentially Private Item Counts
summary: When purchases cannot be linked to the recommendations users saw, item-level purchase counts still constrain the comparison: bounds on the metric difference over all count-consistent assignments, computed with a reduced transportation network, with a joint confidence guarantee for differentially private counts. On two e-commerce cohorts the counts settle comparisons mostly when a popularity-favouring ranker is involved.

title: Generalization Bounds for Neural Networks with Sparse Connectivity
summary: Generalization bounds for deep nets whose layer weights have l_p quasi-norm constraints (0<p<=1), interpolating between norm-based and parameter-counting bounds; as p->0 the bound scales with the square root of the number of active parameters, tighter than parameter counting.

title: High-dimensional limit theorems for adaptive variants of SGD I: Ballistic limits
summary: High-dimensional effective (ballistic) dynamics for Adam, Muon and variants, treating the moving averages and preconditioning by averaging. Applies to tensor PCA, Gaussian single/multi-index models, teacher-student and XOR; shows online SGD generalizing better than Adam early before the curves cross, and proves an Edge-of-Stability statement via an infinity-Laplacian analogue.

title: On the Convergence of Continuous-Time AdamW
summary: Long-time behaviour of continuous-time AdamW with bias correction and fixed weight decay: trajectories are bounded for small decay and approach a locally invariant manifold of dimension equal to the Hessian nullity; with at most one degenerate direction they converge to a point, with two they can move persistently even for a strictly convex objective with a unique minimum.

title: CARE: Contrastive-Anchored Residual Encoding with Listwise Reconstruction for Retrieval-Oriented Semantic IDs
summary: Two retrieval-oriented semantic-ID tokenizers: CARE-SID quantizes after a contrastively trained residual alignment with an anchor loss; CARE-LR also distills the query's similarity distribution over candidates into the SID reconstructions. SIDs are judged without training a generator, by recall when the SID is used as a partition (bucketing view) or as a reconstruction. The embedding matters far more than the quantizer. Deployed in an industrial video search GR stage.

title: Keep it Simple! A Multiple-Choice Task can Benefit Generative Recommendation
summary: Adds a multiple-choice auxiliary task (pick the positive among sampled candidates) to TIGER-style semantic-ID generative recommendation, so the model sees negatives and relative rankings as in BPR; with an information-theoretic and compositional-generalization argument. Gains of 4.9-79% NDCG@10 over TIGER on four datasets.

title: UniGraph: A Unified Graph-based Index for Dynamic Hybrid Dense-Sparse Vector Retrieval
summary: UniGraph merges graph neighbour sets computed at several dense/sparse hybrid weights into one bounded-degree index, so a single graph serves query-specific hybrid weights; weight-guided entry points and dense-first pruning. 27.6-52.3% higher QPS at Recall@100>=0.95 in the mixed-weight setting; deployed at Ant Group.

title: HorizANN: Elastically Scaling Vector Search with Ghost Edges
summary: HorizANN: distributed graph-based ANN that repartitions without rebuilding indexes, keeping 'ghost edges' across moved partition boundaries; scales from 100M vectors on one worker to 1B on ten at ~3.4K QPS and 0.998 Recall@10.

title: CapCover Filter: Semantic Approximate Membership Queries over Embeddings
summary: CapCover Filter answers 'is any stored embedding within cosine threshold t?' without false negatives, by covering the set with spherical caps; one filter serves any threshold. At t=0.95 it skips 20-100% of index accesses with 2% of FP32 memory, up to 382% higher throughput in front of FAISS flat.

title: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search
summary: Repo-Premium, a repository-level code-search benchmark (91 repos, PRs 2022-2026). The reported dense-over-BM25 advantage comes largely from evaluation choices (chunked BM25, counting edited tests) and from queries lacking the code's rare identifiers; LLM-generated identifiers plus grep lets BM25 match dense retrieval in every Python pool.

title: When Does Label-Free Deconfounding of Document Embeddings Work?
summary: Systematic study of label-free removal of spurious attributes from document embeddings: simple geometric methods recover much of supervised erasure; failures come from poor proxy-confounder alignment or insufficient coverage; reduced linear recoverability can coexist with high nonlinear recoverability.

title: Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
summary: Demonstration selection as sparse reconstruction of the query representation (matching-pursuit style RES). Across 7 benchmarks and 8 LLMs no selector wins everywhere; RES beats MMR on 34/56 pairs, relevance retrieval stays strong on template-heavy tasks, and the best representation layer depends on the selector.

title: StaleBench: Isolating Stale Retrieval in Agent Memory, and Pricing the Fix
summary: StaleBench: 892 real updating facts (Wikidata validity via TempLAMA) to isolate retrieval of outdated versions in agent memory. Retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards (identical rank-1 results, 29.5-65.6 point reader-accuracy gaps); proposes Contamination@5 and compares Mem0, Graphiti, LangMem and ERASE.

title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
summary: Label-free audit of LLM recommenders: candidate descriptions rewritten by randomly assigned paraphrasers; if choices are invariant, every paraphraser is chosen equally often, giving a test without relevance labels. Across 9 LLMs and 20k queries, longer descriptions raise selection odds by up to 38% per SD of length.

title: Exploration of Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation Models
summary: Logit-gradient view of GRPO-style objectives in generative recommendation: clipping creates dead gradients, negative-advantage updates can blow up with the ratio, and updates ignore absolute confidence. Gradient-Bounded Policy Optimization uses stop-gradient normalisation so updates are always active, sign-symmetrically bounded and vanish as pi->1 for positives / pi->0 for negatives.

title: Learning to Reason with Predictive Gains for Generative Recommendation
summary: GainReason: rewards each reasoning sentence in LLM-based generative recommendation by its Predictive Gain, the change in the target semantic ID's log-likelihood, shown to align in expectation with the ranking objective; sentence-level RL plus an auxiliary task to use the reasoning. Improves over GRPO-based baselines on three benchmarks.

title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
summary: Each pairwise preference loss defines a vector field on the simplex. Projecting onto one preferred/dispreferred pair gives a 1-D margin ODE with closed-form solutions: DPO margins grow like log t, IPO margins converge to 1/(2 tau), label noise turns DPO's margin bounded (a phase transition), and label smoothing gives SimPO a finite attractor. The predictions are checked on five model families.

title: A Transformer-Derived Iterative Preconditioner
summary: A softmax-attention transformer trained in context to solve Xw=y implicitly improves the conditioning of XX^T. The authors extract this into RAPID, a standalone anytime preconditioner for SPD matrices (randomized mixing plus sparse local corrections), and prove convergence to any target condition number in a Haar-mixing idealization, with only logarithmic dependence on the initial conditioning.

title: Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training
summary: Synthetic corpus where every term of the next-token loss can be computed exactly, testing latent two-hop questions whose bridge entity never appears in two-hop training data. Standard and looped transformers fail. A looped 'Baton' variant that passes the bridge entity as a token embedding succeeds under answer-only training, but under full next-token training its accuracy rises and then falls. Splitting the gradient into three terms shows the decline comes from the second hop while both facts are still recalled.

title: Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking
summary: Parallel listwise LLM reranking splits candidates into groups with fixed quotas. Under a simple retriever model, dealing candidates round-robin by retriever rank cuts the fewest true top-10 documents of any equal-quota split, and contiguous chunks get worse as the retriever improves. DealRank is within 0.1 nDCG@10 of the best schedules, and dealing cuts BlitzRank's repair calls from 59% to 14% of queries.

title: Better Rankers, Worse Retrievers: The Hidden Cost of RL Post-Training in Generative Recommendation
summary: On five datasets, RL post-training of semantic-ID generative recommenders raises hit@K for small K but lowers recall at K in the hundreds. Controlled experiments trace this to negative advantages on sampled rollout items: with only one logged next item, RL penalises the model's most plausible alternatives, often other similar users' next items. An 'out-of-rollout anchoring' loss that keeps the SFT ordering outside the rollout restores recall.

title: NONSENSE: Non-Semantic Strings Expose Semanticity Gaps in Dense Retrieval
summary: A black-box sparse-edit attack builds visibly non-semantic strings, with no query-term copying, that maximise dense similarity to a query. On five BEIR-style datasets and three single-vector retrievers, these strings often outscore the best relevant passage and rank first in the whole corpus. Nearest-neighbour status can be separated from meaning.

title: Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers
summary: For looped refiners (HRM/TRM-style) with deep supervision toward one stored answer, the paper proves that puzzles with many valid answers create a loss floor no capacity removes, and that the loss minimiser blends answers into an invalid output. Training each pass toward the nearest correct answer makes correct answers fixed points with a convergence guarantee. Sudoku with 2–64 solutions goes from 2.5% to 98.8% solved.

title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
summary: 'Tree-grams' are n-gram language models whose conditional tensor is a hierarchical composition of order-2/3 tensors, with context n and rank d as explicit knobs. They beat n-gram baselines and come close to transformers. Used as data generators, they make muP hyperparameter transfer more robust, and their entropy and correlation range control post-fine-tuning gaps.

title: A Log-Timescale Perturbation Bound for Selective State Space Models at Every Sequence Length
summary: Measuring timescale perturbations on a log scale gives a hidden-state perturbation bound for selective-scan (Mamba) cells that holds at every sequence length, needs no lower bound on the timescale, and is tight within a factor of about 2. It extends to Mamba's released update when the timescale is bounded above.

title: SOTA or Luck? The Winner's Curse in LLM Leaderboards
summary: Ranking noisy benchmark scores overstates the leaders (a winner's curse). An m-out-of-N bootstrap reduces Theta(N^{-1/2}) ranking bias to o(N^{-1/2}) under separated tiers, and gives rank intervals and consistent tier recovery. On SWE-bench Verified, 13 of 173 models land in the leading tier.

title: On the Kissing Number of Craig's Lattice and Spherical List Decoding
summary: Polynomial-time list decoding of spherical codes from Craig's lattices for angles below 45 degrees. Bacher's omega(n^k) kissing-number lower bound is tight for small k, and an algorithm computes kissing numbers up to dimension 521 (Ducas et al.).

title: SIMQ: A Single Graph-based Index for Multi-Vector Query
summary: A single graph index over data-aware cluster centroids of ColBERT token vectors approximates MaxSim through per-token graph search, with no centroid interaction matrix. Includes an argument that data-aware partitions have lower expected approximation error than data-oblivious ones, under a manifold assumption. Integrated into VSAG.

title: Pelorus: Warped-Product Graph Indexing for Hyperbolic Vector Search
summary: Warped-product proximity graph for hyperbolic ANN. It keeps radial/conformal scalars in FP32, uses 2-bit spherical direction codes, and adds conformal-distortion-motivated debiasing. Reports 4.3–6.3x throughput at 99% Recall@10 on Cohere-1M over full-precision polar graphs.

title: Errpedia: Is Your Exact $k$-NN Vector Search Really Exact?
summary: Errpedia: 1,616 queries in 21 error categories, with ground truth from exact rational arithmetic, testing whether 'exact' k-NN search is exact. All 20 tested library and database configurations return wrong top-10 sets on some queries, from floating-point rounding and overflow.

title: Efficient Wide-Beam Generative Retrieval with Model-Native Trie Decoding and Shared-Context Attention
summary: LinkedIn serves wide-beam trie-constrained GR with a GPU-native trie output head and attention over shared prompt KV across beams. Up to 5.6x throughput at beam width 200 over a Python logit-processor baseline.

title: IntentGR: Enhancing Intent for End-to-End Personalized Generative Retrieval in Search
summary: End-to-end personalized GR for search that injects query-level behavioural evidence into SID learning, alignment, long-tail enrichment and decoding. +8–12% Recall@10 on AOL4PS and an industrial dataset, with the largest gains on long-tail queries.

title: Fair Bubble Sort: Provably Optimal Fair Ranking with Continuous Sensitive Attributes
summary: Fair ranking with a continuous protected attribute, using a Kendall-correlation parity constraint and minimal Kemeny distance. An adjacent-swap algorithm is exactly optimal for unweighted Kemeny distance and approximate in the score-weighted case.

title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
summary: In long-tailed multi-label classification, rare labels are often recovered from frequent co-occurring 'companion' labels rather than learned. The paper defines a within-label estimand of this dependence and a training-label statistic that bounds, before training, how much reported recall can exceed companion-free recall. Up to 18% of credited tail true positives depend on companions.

title: Lost in the Funnel: Selection-Induced Miscalibration in Ranking and Decision Systems
summary: Scores calibrated where a model produces them lose calibration after selection in multi-stage ranking funnels. A boundary-wise residual-identity diagnosis attributes this to selection, not model error, and selection-aware recalibration at the decision boundary cuts decision-time ECE by 60–80% in production.

title: KVUse: Reusable-KV User Memory for Efficient LLM Recommenders
summary: Meta stores LLM-recommender user profiles as reusable KV caches, written by LoRA writers trained by self-distillation, instead of text. Ranking calls skip re-prefilling them: 4–4.5x scoring throughput with no significant quality change.

title: Cluster-Guided Decoding with Trust-Region Constraints for Personalized Recommendation
summary: Amazon learns a hierarchy of semantic item clusters and adds a cluster-level prior directly to item scores. The prior stays defined for cold-start users. Gains in Recall and nDCG over classical, neural and LLM baselines.

title: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't
summary: A minimal RAG memory (hybrid BM25+cosine, chronological notes) matches prior state of the art on LongMemEval-S and BEAM. New probes where the agent must apply a remembered rule show that no memory design wins everywhere.

title: More Than a Score: Reinforcement Learning with Verbalized Feedback for Generative Recommendation
summary: Tencent's VerRec: during RL for generative recommendation, a simulated user writes feedback in words on each candidate. The policy refines its pick, and original and refined candidates are trained jointly with GRPO.

title: From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search
summary: Tencent Yuanbao trains retrieval, ranking and document-set selection against one per-query rubric, aiming for documents that are useful to an LLM rather than relevant one at a time. +8.5% end-to-end answer quality online.

title: MIPR: A Benchmark for Reasoning-Intensive Multimodal Intent-to-Product Retrieval with Multi-Category Solutions
summary: MIPR: an Alibaba benchmark of 3,522 multimodal shopping-intent queries over 30k products, where one intent can be met by several product categories. The best embedding retriever reaches 49% nDCG@10.

title: When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?
summary: Running a multimodal embedding model's layers again helps little unless information can flow from query to image. The paper proves that an image placed before the query stays query-independent under forward-only recurrence. A model pretrained with recurrence gains +4.2 on MMEB-V2.

title: Intrinsic Attention as Navigator: A Non-Generative Retrieval Method for Multi-Hop Queries
summary: Training-free multi-hop retriever. It reads bridging clues from the embedding model's attention, subtracts revealed clues from the query vector, and reranks toward the next-hop evidence.

title: TokenFormer V2: Breaking the Resolution-Complexity Dilemma in Unified Recommendation
summary: Tencent's TokenFormer V2 keeps a token for every user behaviour, attends within groups merged hierarchically, and lets the final readout access each token directly. 5x fewer FLOPs than baselines and +2.3% GMV online.

title: CLEAR: Legible and Steerable Recommendation via Grounded Natural-Language Interests
summary: Meta's CLEAR exposes inferred user interests as editable natural-language objects. Each interest drives lexical, behavioural and embedding retrieval, ranking and exposure control. Deployed on Instagram and Facebook.

title: Reflection Is Not Always Worth It: Budgeted Reflection Allocation for Recommendation Agents
summary: Uses cheap uncertainty signals to decide which users get costly training-time LLM reflection in recommendation agents.

title: DetouR: Plugging Association Routes into Search Agents for Multi-hop Question Answering
summary: DetouR lets search agents follow hyperlinks from retrieved pages, using a learned link scorer and personalized PageRank context selection. It reaches evidence the question never names, with no extra search or LLM calls. +4 EM on 2Wiki.

title: EchoSpec: Training Search Agents to Weigh Evidence Above Echoes
summary: RL-trained search agents treat paraphrased copies of a false claim as independent sources: eight echoes overturn 58–73% of correct answers. EchoSpec trains agents to seek primary evidence and to abstain without it.

title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
summary: Ranks stored agent memories by an LLM's judgement of usefulness to the question instead of embedding similarity. Gold memory is ranked first in 85% of InMind indirect queries, against 0–2% for BM25 and MiniLM.

title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
summary: Treats RAG query rewriting as black-box optimisation over prompt templates and decoding settings, using global and local search plus an elite memory pool.

title: Which Tokens, in What Order, and How Fast? A Theoretical Analysis of On-Policy Distillation Objectives
summary: Theory of on-policy distillation objectives. Sequence-level OPD has a 'future agreement bias' that makes it fit the teacher at later token positions first and can push early positions toward tokens the teacher finds improbable; token-level objectives avoid this. Forward KL gives a well-behaved landscape, while reverse KL and other f-divergences can have vanishing gradients even far from the teacher.

title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
summary: Test-time symmetrization: run the model on rewritings of the input (a group G of equivalent representations, e.g. node relabelings) and aggregate. Proves that repeated sampling from one representation cannot replace rewriting, that O(log|G|) random rewritings recover the information of all |G| (uniformly over models, decoders and traces), and that log scaling is optimal; confirmed on four 7-14B models.

title: What Interpolators Store and What They Express: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Benign Overfitting and Label-Free Model Selection
summary: Splits what an interpolating learner does with its sample into storage (information about training labels kept in the model) and expression (information that reaches predictions at fresh inputs). Every interpolator stores exactly nH(Y|X) bits of label noise, so storage-based (incl. CMI) bounds cannot separate interpolators; excess risk is bounded above and below by expressed information, and benign overfitting is vanishing expression. The quantity also gives a label-free model-selection rule.

title: Stability Does Not Mirror Plasticity: A Module-Level View of Declarative and Procedural Learning in Transformers
summary: In a controlled synthetic setup, MLPs are the most plastic modules for declarative memorization and QK/VO projections for procedural tasks. Stability does not mirror this: learning a new procedure by updating QK keeps over half of the stored facts, updating MLPs keeps far less, updating VO loses about four fifths. Reset-and-recovery experiments explain the asymmetry by how other modules depend on each one.

title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
summary: Withholding the training signal for one skill (chess check responses, Othello, bracket languages, molecular strings, a programming language in a 7B model) only delays it: general progress on the rest of the data substitutes for the withheld data, the delay in large models is predictable from small ones, and the data needed to acquire the skill later shrinks as the model improves. A control rule of equal difficulty is learned much more slowly.

title: Differentiable Exact Learning
summary: Couples a state-tracking neural controller (differentiable finite-state transducers, also RNNs/GRUs) with an unbounded external environment, trained on traces that expose observations and actions but hide states. Tiny datasets give extreme length generalization on arithmetic and universal simulation, and argmax over transitions provably yields controllers that exactly implement the target algorithms (under stated assumptions).

title: Two is better than one: optimizing binary rating scales for online platforms
summary: Designing binary rating questions to rank items under inflated feedback: splitting one rating scale into two always improves item ranking; the optimal set of scales is a series of 0-1 step functions with evenly spaced thresholds; adaptive scales chosen from earlier responses give exponentially greater distinguishing power.

title: Improved Leverage Score Sampling for Constrained Active Linear Regression
summary: Active constrained least squares: ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores give query complexity O(d_eff(C) log d / eps^2), with d_eff(C) an anisotropic effective dimension of the constraint set, improved to 1/eps for convex constraints; matching lower bounds show d/eps^2 is unavoidable without convexity.

title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
summary: Two-layer networks trained by SGD on a multi-index teacher in the proportional limit: first-layer weights orthogonal to the teacher subspace develop teacher-dependent spectral spikes in their Gram matrix, which inflate representation variance and hurt generalization. A tractable surrogate ('Decomposed Dynamics') has the same asymptotic test error as SGD; freezing the orthogonal part helps.

title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses
summary: Avoiding path-space analysis, the error of a diffusion sampler with an imperfect score need not accumulate polynomially with the horizon when the target satisfies a Poincare inequality; more generally the error is controlled in a weaker metric for any target. Given a score-error bound and a Poincare constant, the sampler is nearly information-theoretically optimal in TV.

title: Rare-Tail Statistics For Learning Biased Gaussian Halfspaces with Label Noise
summary: Learning biased Gaussian halfspaces under label noise: averaging only the minority class (rare-tail mean) recovers the direction at the information-theoretic sample rate in the large-bias regime, where global first-moment methods are provably suboptimal, under probit and slowly decaying margin noise.

title: Monoculture Robust Learning
summary: Monoculture robustness in PAC learning: from one dataset, output k accurate hypotheses whose joint failure is comparable to training on k independent datasets. If the base learner is rho-replicable, k independent runs on the same sample drive the individual conjunctive error down exponentially in k; a lower bound shows a sample-size multiplier Omega(log 1/gamma) can be necessary.

title: Nearly Tight Almost Sure Convergence Rates for the Last iterate of SGD
summary: Almost-sure last-iterate rates for SGD on convex objectives: k^{-1/3} for smooth objectives with a stationary minimizer, k^{-1/4} otherwise and for nonsmooth objectives, with anytime step sizes, and matching lower bounds up to logs.

title: The Spectral Distribution of Matrix Least Squares Solutions, and the Ellipsoid Fitting Problem
summary: Closed-form support of the spectral distribution of the least-squares solution to a random linear system in a symmetric matrix. Application to ellipsoid fitting through n Gaussian points in R^d: the least-squares candidate is PSD only up to n ~ d^2/10 (proving a statistical-physics prediction) and its dual certificate up to n ~ 2d^2/5, below the true threshold d^2/4.

title: Copying along Arithmetic Progressions Cannot Simulate Interleaving with Polylogarithmic Loss
summary: Answers Kosoy's question on compressing words by interleaving: arithmetic repetition systems are within a factor 2n^{1/4} of the smallest zipline program, and some binary words need n^{1/4-o(1)}, so the optimal exponent is 1/4, not 1/3. This rules out a polylog mistake bound for Kosoy's polynomial-time next-letter predictor via this route.

title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling
summary: ExecJudges: a frontier LLM writes, per TREC topic, an executable lexical program that labels relevance. Agreement with NIST assessors matches LLM judges on TREC DL 2019-2021, ranks official runs with Kendall's tau 0.87-0.94, at $0.17-0.49 per topic once.

title: Optimize the Cob, Then the Kernel: Optimizing Beam Search for Generative Recommendation Inference
summary: Serving generative recommenders: tree attention over beams to avoid repeated KV reads of the shared prefix, static KV allocation, unrolled generation and constrained decoding give up to 25x lower latency than vLLM on Ascend NPUs without custom kernels.

title: CONCORD-Rec: Catalog-Conditioned Modality Utility for Semantic-ID Diffusion Recommendation
summary: Discrete-diffusion recommender over semantic IDs with a reliability gate on modalities, trained from counterfactual catalog-partition utility; robust to missing or conflicting modalities (+4% NDCG overall, +14.6% under 30% conflict).

title: VIBRA: Backward-Compatible Cross-Modal Retrieval with Consensus Barycenters
summary: Backward-compatible cross-modal retrieval: train the new encoder to match a barycenter of several old-space views, with a margin argument for when the barycenter helps; best compatible method in 50 upgrade settings among CLIP/SigLIP2 backbones.

title: X-split Argus: Learning Reusable History Tokens for Efficient CTR Prediction
summary: Ad ranking that compresses long user histories offline into reusable tokens and scores candidates by cross-attention, trained end to end with distillation from an uncompressed teacher; online gains in a production bidding system.

title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
summary: Synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, generated by a fine-tuned Llama 3.2 3B and annotated with entities, released for medical IR research; evaluated for utility, fidelity, diversity and privacy.

title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
summary: KnowMe Paper Radar: a paper-recommendation tool combining topical relevance, recency, author histories and collaboration paths with inspectable score components; cached abstracts raise NDCG@10 from 0.41 to 0.60 on expert-judged tasks.

title: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity
summary: In a solvable high-dimensional model of multi-head attention, head specialization is a true phase transition in the number of samples (a non-analyticity of the test error). Depending on data structure and regularization it can go through an uninformative differentiation phase or a cascade of transitions that recover progressively weaker latent features; the paper links these statistical transitions to the stagewise emergence of heads in online training. BERT syntactic heads also appear only above a data-size threshold.

title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
summary: Proves that adaptive beam search with relaxation gamma on alpha-reachable graphs (DiskANN slow preprocessing) is an (alpha+1)/(alpha(gamma+1)-1)-approximation in any metric, unifying Indyk-Xu (greedy, gamma=0) and Al-Jazzazi et al. (navigable graphs); a tighter bound holds on sorted alpha-reachable graphs in l2. A learned beam predictor built on the analysis cuts SSD query latency by up to 30% versus classical beam search at matched recall on 100M-point sets.

title: Is a Description Worth a Thousand Demonstrations? Specificity and Reliability of Task Descriptions in In-Context Learning
summary: Models a task description in ICL as an informative prior with a specificity and a reliability, and measures its value as an effective sample size (number of demonstrations it is worth). For in-context linear regression, a reliable description's ESS grows with its specificity and with the task dimension, while a possibly irrelevant one gains little from specificity unless demonstrations are present. Meta-trained transformers come close to the Bayes-optimal ESS; pretrained LMs underuse specific descriptions unless reasoning is enabled.

title: LQ-Rec: Late Quantization for Sequential Recommendation
summary: Late Quantization: keep the sequential-recommendation encoder and scoring in continuous space and quantize only the item side into semantic IDs from an end-to-end residual quantizer, decoded non-autoregressively. An additive error decomposition and a pairwise-ordering theorem bound the ranking drop caused by quantization; ranking improves monotonically with SID length (unlike autoregressive GR) and one model supports anytime compression.

title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
summary: Constructs a sample compression scheme of size O(d^2 log^2 d) for every binary class of VC dimension d, proving the weak (polynomial) form of the Floyd-Warmuth sample compression conjecture; the previous best bound depending only on d (Moran-Yehudayoff 2016) was exponential.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
summary: 64 from-scratch pretraining runs (1.3-8B parameters, 1-2T tokens) of transformers and linear models. Canon layers (local token mixing) save about 30% of tokens at 8B; with Canon, plain gated linear attention matches Gated DeltaNet and beats Mamba2. Linear models that match transformers on benchmarks still fail to retrieve from a 500-token context, and no model reliably solves a short two-hop question; small synthetic playgrounds predicted these differences at <100M parameters.

title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
summary: Formalizes diverse generation as sampling a K-subset of strings from a determinantal point process (quality from the LM likelihood, repulsion from embedding geometry). PoolDPP importance-weights a finite candidate pool and runs a K-DPP on it; the KL to the target K-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size with an explicit constant. Improves quality-diversity and precision-recall frontiers on open-ended generation and ambiguous text-to-SQL.

title: Generative News Recommendation Reproduces Popularity: A Memorization-Based Analysis
summary: Continually trains Llama 3 8B on ~20M Japanese news sessions to generate the next article title. Generated titles are more concentrated than the logs; frequently repeated target titles are memorized more (verbatim and approximately), and more memorized titles are produced for a wider range of prompts. Target-level deduplication lowers both memorization and concentration, at a large accuracy cost.

title: When Do Rankings Beat Signs? Gradient Direction Recovery under Even Nuisance
summary: Asks when ranking a batch of antipodal query pairs recovers a gradient direction with fewer evaluations than within-pair signs, for a linear signal plus an unknown even nuisance. Under small relative shell variation, a reversed-order decoder reaches angular accuracy eps with O~(d + sqrt(d/eps)) evaluations in one round, matching a lower bound, versus Theta(d/eps) for sign-only feedback; multi-round minimax rates are given for quadratics.

title: Sequential Probability Assignment against Smoothed Adversaries with Unknown Base Measure
summary: Sequential probability assignment (online log loss) against smoothed adversaries when the base measure is unknown, without Lipschitz assumptions. Regret bounds use empirical l_inf Hellinger entropy (adaptive adversary) and l_2 Hellinger entropy (oblivious), via truncated empirical Hellinger covers; a lower bound shows tightness for natural classes and separates the known- and unknown-base-measure regimes.

title: The low-degree sample complexity of clustering Gaussian mixtures with more groups than dimensions
summary: Characterizes, up to subpolynomial factors, the minimal separation for clustering a mixture of K isotropic Gaussians in R^d with low-degree polynomials when K > d (normally distributed centers). For K = d^{p/2}, recovering the clustering at subpolynomial separation needs about K^3 d^{(ceil(p)-p)/2} samples, and this suffices when p is not an integer.

title: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions
summary: For jump diffusions on embeddings of categorical data, studies leave-one-out prediction (each coordinate predicted from the corrupted others). Proves that with complete coordinate resets and state-independent clocks, exact LOO reset probabilities plus the full endpoint-posterior drift preserve the prescribed marginals, and that the drift can be completed analytically from LOO probabilities. LOO variants improve generation on Text8, LM1B and ZINC250k.

title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
summary: Compares linear probes with models' own answers (signal detection theory) in six base/post-trained pairs. On human-vs-AI authorship judgments, probes separate the classes while answers do not and post-training lowers answer sensitivity; on negation truth, post-training instead repairs readout. The change happens in SFT and sits at positions after the text from mid-depth on; 2,000 labelled examples can set the readout direction.

title: Standardized Tolerance for Adaptive Reuse and Repair: A Method for HNSW Migration Under Embedding Model Change Scenarios
summary: STARR migrates an HNSW index after an embedding-model change by reusing source edges whose standardized length stays within a tolerance, with bounds on edge rejection under local distortion and a repair pass guaranteeing reachability. Median 16.7x faster than rebuilding across 240 MS MARCO model transitions, about 1 point recall loss.

title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
summary: CACO post-trains flow-matching/diffusion generative retrievers so that the multiple sampled ANN queries cover complementary items, using a label-free coverage objective and an unbiased gradient estimator through non-differentiable ANN search. Up to +24% Recall@100/400 and half the inter-query overlap at 0.5-3% extra latency.

title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving High-Dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
summary: ObliSC: ANN search over a public vector database with private queries, fully oblivious to access patterns, with parallel optimizations; competitive efficiency and recall with a light index on six benchmarks.

title: CAIMS: Scalable Cross-Array In-Memory Search
summary: CAIMS: top-k similarity search across many content-addressable memory arrays by turning local threshold matches into global coarse scores and reducing hierarchically; on a 3D NAND model for RAG retrieval, up to 22x throughput and 427x energy efficiency over a server CPU.

title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
summary: DiLE: universal multimodal embedding model with learnable latent queries, shared-private experts and on-policy hard-negative distillation (reverse KL to a teacher over the student's own confusable candidates); state of the art on MMEB-v2, UVRB and MRMR.

title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
summary: Meta: whole-page generative re-ranking trained with a local page-level policy-improvement objective that splits exactly into one target per position, each comparing candidates by the score of the complete page they lead to; beats generative re-ranking baselines on KuaiRand, RL4RS and logged industrial pages.

title: DNA: Unlocking Depth Scaling in CTR Models
summary: Taobao: stacking cross-attention layers over user behavior sequences saturates because every layer reads the same keys/values; DNA lets the behavior sequence update from the request at each layer (still linear in length), giving +0.08-0.26 AUC at equal FLOPs and +0.8% CTR online.

title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
summary: LINEAGE: benchmark for retrieving the prior papers a paper uses as empirical baselines, built as lineage graphs over 121k AI papers (165k edges, 80k queries); 19 retrievers degrade sharply with lineage distance.

title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
summary: Meta: sets per-table pruning ratios for in-training embedding pruning from feature importance instead of table size, cutting 20-40% of embedding memory at equal or better accuracy and saving 1,000+ GPU-hours per launch; reproduced on DLRM/Criteo.

title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
summary: AutoRAGBench: nine tasks where LLM agents build RAG systems from scratch in six H800-hours; the best agent configuration averages 56.1 against a composite human-SOTA of 44.4.

title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
summary: Meta: LLM agents propose and tune feature selections for a fleet of ads ranking models under shared pipeline-cost and per-model QPS budgets; +0.31% normalized entropy offline, 2.3% lower pipeline cost, +0.20% online.

title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
summary: Evidence-based credit assignment for RL-trained search agents: a training-only reward scoring each search by how much its retrieved documents raise the likelihood of the reference answer under an evidence-only prompt, so learning continues when all rollouts fail; +1 to +4.8 EM over GRPO on seven search-QA sets.

title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
summary: Meta: human-on-the-loop LLM agents propose, implement, train and evaluate changes to large search rankers; one campaign ran 1,097 experiments, accepted 325, and its best model raised search volume by 0.23% online.

title: MARS Technical Report
summary: Taobao MARS: a fine-tuned 0.6B LLM sets per-user pipeline configurations (retrieval quotas, model choice, fusion weights, reranker settings) near-line, trained with SFT, preference optimization and sandboxed GRPO; up to +7.3% GMV in A/B tests.

title: Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?
summary: A Transformer pretrained on simulated datasets, with the true parameter as label, learns the posterior mean and covariance of a queried estimand. They prove that under locally flat priors of slowly growing complexity the posterior mean is semiparametrically efficient for every estimand, and the Transformer inherits efficiency with asymptotically exact Wald coverage, even under distribution shift; a fixed data-generating distribution makes pretraining much harder.

title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
summary: Develops a theory of how predictive information is distributed over a text's history via the scaling of a family of information measures; self-similar organization predicts a collapse of these measures across lengths, which they observe in long documents. Predictive information is present at every measured scale, a stronger statement than long-range dependence.

title: Renormalized Entropy from Symmetries: Simplicity Bias and Neural Heat Death
summary: Computes the equilibrium distribution over represented functions under Langevin dynamics with vanishing Gaussian regularization, isolating the effect of parameter symmetries. A renormalized entropy appears at positive temperature: for linear networks it favors singular and low-rank functions, for homogeneous activations it favors dead neurons, up to a 'heat death' of vanishing output.

title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
summary: PhD thesis: diffusion models behave as associative memories whose per-sample basins shrink as data grows, with spurious attractors marking the onset of generation; uniform-state discrete diffusion LMs show basins around unseen sentences expanding while training-sample basins contract, and conditional entropy locates a model on this transition.

title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
summary: Across 12 LLMs, native coordinate axes align better with other models, brain responses and linguistic features than random rotations with the same geometry, but well short of the best rotation: LLM axes are partially canonical.

title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
summary: Tracks self-generated hallucinations during reasoning-style RL on knowledge tasks across six open models: rewarded hallucinations are recalled 4.83% more later (0.17% for unrewarded ones), even facts the model retracted in its own chain; memorization is strongest on the hardest questions and reduces later abstention.

title: How Language Models Compress and Compare: Understanding Selection with Token Covariance Maps
summary: Token covariance maps across depth show a compress-then-compare organization for selection prompts (incl. pairwise reranking) in 14 decoder models: diffuse early layers, a shared low-rank bottleneck mid-depth, then re-expansion into option-option geometry; it emerges during training and intervening at the bottleneck disrupts later comparison.

title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
summary: Learning-dynamics analysis of on-policy distillation: identifies states where sampled-token updates cannot fix teacher-student mismatch (low student mass on the teacher's top-p set), shows their gradients interfere with other tokens, and traces how a termination-token mismatch drives repetitive, over-long generations.

title: Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning
summary: Across 361 corruption settings of GSM8K SFT traces, GRPO restores accuracy to the gold baseline; eight wrong three-line 'form-only' traces as SFT init beat gold SFT after RL, and SFT accuracy is uncorrelated with post-RL accuracy: SFT sets form, RL finds function.

title: How Far Does Lossless Re-tokenization Move an RLVR Update?
summary: Re-tokenizing the same RLVR rollouts (splitting ~1 token in 25) moves the update 0.556 times as far as using a different batch, in a consistent direction; in a tabular model they prove only the zero step agrees across tokenizations. Real re-encoding touches few tokens and the effect on accuracy is not significant.

title: A preference for local interaction between layers emerges during training
summary: Perturbing one layer and measuring the response in others across 512 five-layer networks on modular addition: inter-layer responses grow during training and become ordered by distance, so locality between layers emerges although the loss couples all layers.

title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
summary: An exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition isolates computation that appears only when a set of layers acts together; across Pythia, OLMo and Amber checkpoints this connected coordination grows during pretraining, matters causally for perplexity, and is negatively correlated with layer similarity.

title: Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining
summary: 39 1B models pretrained with only the tokenizer varied: better vocabulary allocation raises cross-lingual alignment in early-mid layers and knowledge sharing in FFN neurons, yet cross-lingual transfer stays unchanged; cross-script transfer remains low even with fair allocation.

title: How Many Bytes Has a BPE Model Seen? Estimating Byte-Token Exposure in Pretraining from Corpus Statistics and Embedding Norms
summary: Estimates how often byte-fallback tokens were seen in BPE pretraining from corpus statistics and from embedding/unembedding row norms, calibrated with untrained padding rows; never-valid UTF-8 bytes stay at initialization, and the norm-frequency relation folds at high frequency.

title: Distillation with Errors: Sparse Unbiased Backpropagation for Knowledge Distillation
summary: Distillation with Errors: uses the zero-sum structure of logit gradients to build sparse paired estimates whose expectation equals the full-vocabulary KD gradient (proved unbiased), with geometry-aware pairing and stratified sampling to cut variance; up to 2.2x output-head speedup.

title: Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models
summary: Frontier models asked to edit a weaker LM's weights from examples mostly write the ICL task vector (few-shot minus zero-shot residual at the last token) into near-silent MLP units keyed to the prompt format, matching ICL and LoRA accuracy but brittle to rewording.

title: Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures
summary: Tasklets: a shared benchmark of small synthetic tasks (recall, sequence manipulation, state tracking) for comparing sequence-mixing layers under one setup, with controlled small-model comparisons.

title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
summary: A deterministic agnostic PAC learner for partial concept classes of VC dimension d with O((d+log(1/δ))/ε²) samples, matching the Alon et al. (FOCS 2021) lower bound.

title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
summary: Black-box reduction (empirical residual pruning) turning finite-variance regression into a procedure for noise with only an unknown α-moment, α∈(1,2): rate ν^{1/α}((d+log 1/δ)/n)^{(α-1)/α} in Σ-norm without knowing α, with a matching minimax lower bound.

title: Minimax-Optimal Small-Loss Regret in Online Convex Optimization and Applications to Contextual Search and Online Inverse Optimization
summary: OCO with one subgradient per round achieving minimax-optimal small-loss regret O(1+√Δ*) without smoothness or knowing Δ*; consequences include resolving the Θ(√d/κ²) rate for contextual search with biased comparison flips.

title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning
summary: For flow matching on a finite training set, late-time trajectories contract exponentially toward the nearest training sample away from Voronoi interfaces, with sharp Wasserstein error rates in the restart noise; connects flow matching and score-based diffusion through this limiting geometry.

title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
summary: Introduces the 'critical thalweg', a structure containing all critical points of the linear-network loss, gives a geometric proof of Baldi-Hornik under weaker assumptions, and observes GD is attracted to it.

title: Verifying and Strengthening Neural Tangent Kernel Theory
summary: Lean 4 formalization of NTK convergence for two-layer tanh networks under gradient flow, plus sharper concentration-width constants and an L2 parameter geometry fix for the linearization bound; required widths stay impractical.

title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
summary: Google: query a vector index built with another embedding model without re-embedding, via a small anchor set chosen by cosine farthest-point sampling, an adapter with orthogonality regularization, and a router that sends hard queries to the original encoder; up to +35% nDCG@10 on BEIR.
