title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
summary: Augments pretraining text with search queries and locally retrieved results so LMs learn to issue and use search during pretraining; a 1.4B model matches a FLOP-matched 3.3B baseline on knowledge tasks and the gain survives SFT (Raffel, Jaggi).

title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
summary: Meta: K learnable tokens linked by a residual recurrence in one forward pass for multimodal retrieval and generation, with a reachability/one-step-descent argument; matches looped models at much lower latency.

title: LongCat Recall Sparse Attention: Co-Designing Key Organization and Retrieval for Long-Context Inference
summary: Meituan: retrieval-based sparse attention with an incrementally maintained paged index (time buckets, capacity-balanced directional groups with per-group centers) for top-K key selection; 4.7x faster selection than DSA at 1M tokens.

title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking
summary: VK: a DCNv2-style cross layer with a division branch that represents Laurent monomials (ratios), removing hand-built ratio features from a production short-video ranker with significant A/B gains.

title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
summary: Self-improvement loop for multimodal search agents that grows new tasks together with their evidence in the retrieval backend, so correct searches are not penalized for missing evidence; +9.8 points on nine benchmarks.

title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
summary: Interpretable embeddings whose coordinates are calibrated yes/no/not-stated answers to natural-language questions; similarity decomposes per question, new questions extend the index without re-encoding, and retrieval matches dense candidate generation for entity matching.

title: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage-Abuse Attacks on Encrypted Vector Search
summary: Leakage-abuse attack on encrypted vector search: co-retrieval access patterns form a graph whose spectral groups reveal record labels and query categories (up to 84% label accuracy with 1% known labels), also under an encrypted approximate scheme.

title: Space-Efficient Text Indexing for Advanced Counting Queries
summary: Compact text indexes (O(n log σ) bits) answering a general class of advanced counting queries in optimal or near-optimal time, improving on MAST-style indexes for non-overlapping occurrence counting.

title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
summary: Extended version of an ICTIR '21 short paper: ranking candidate team leaders by combining technical fit, managerial knowledge and communication in a probabilistic model, with one metric per quality, on Stack Overflow collections.

title: Training Dynamics of Large State-Transition Models
summary: Next-token prediction with a one-token context (a 'state-transition model') where input and output embeddings of dimension d < V are trained jointly from Gaussian init by perturbed GD with weight decay on population cross-entropy. For a low-rank centred log-probability table, the untied model reaches relative prediction gain > 7/8 once d = Ω(√V); the tied model gets 1 − O(V/d²) on observed states plus a transfer guarantee to unseen states. The key tool is a bound on the trace of the softmax-CE Hessian at approximate second-order stationary points.

title: Grammar Sparsity Sets How Transformers Learn Random Languages
summary: Transformers trained on the Random Language Model (random hierarchical grammar with known conditional entropies). Dense grammars are learnt level by level: sibling-based prediction after t ∝ V steps, full-context only after t ∝ V^3, with a widening plateau in between; sparse grammars are learnt all at once at t ∝ √V. The exponents 1 and 1/2 are derived at depth one for a linear model trained with Adam.

title: Statistical mechanics of linear classification on hierarchical tree data
summary: A linear classifier is trained to infer the root of a broadcast process on a tree from its N leaves. Keeping the exact non-Gaussian law along the label direction and treating transverse fluctuations as Gaussian gives a finite-depth replica theory that matches learning curves. At large depth there is a double descent whose first descent occurs at N^ω samples (0<ω<1) and whose overfitting peak occurs at order N.

title: Vanishing Initialization Turns Diagonal Tensor Gradient Flow into Greedy Matching
summary: Gradient flow on CP tensor factorization (order ≥ 3, diagonal target in orthonormal bases) from vanishing initialization is proved to follow a greedy bipartite matching between model atoms and target components, ordered by initialization-dependent activation clocks, giving a staircase loss. Modular addition fits after Fourier diagonalization, yielding an explicit distribution-free large-system loss curve.

title: Global Stability and Loss Convergence in Matrix Factorization
summary: For L(X,Y) = f(XY) with convex, smooth, Lipschitz-gradient f (including cross-entropy) and a minimizing set compact modulo invariances, GD with a learning rate below a positive threshold keeps parameters bounded, has summable squared gradients and converges in loss from every finite initialization. The proof uses a decreasing imbalance quantity between the two factors.

title: Grokking as a Subspace Search: Computing the Destination Before Training
summary: On group tasks, the low-dimensional embedding subspace a grokking network ends in can be computed from the task before training and is shown to be essentially unique. Giving the network this subspace removes the delay; removing it caps accuracy at a precomputable ceiling; during normal training embeddings drift toward it long before test accuracy rises.

title: Pretraining Representation Lottery Determines Fine-tuning Generalization
summary: In a synthetic setup with known concept geometry, seeds with equal pretraining loss differ widely in fine-tuning generalization. Injecting the true geometry, or distilling a lucky seed's representation (not its behaviour) into an unlucky one, fixes fine-tuning; reproduced on multi-seed Pythia-160M/410M, where the transferable representation lives in deep layers.

title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View
summary: Treats LLM pretraining as a non-autonomous dynamical system over weights and Adam states. At sensitive checkpoints a 1e-5 weight perturbation yields 35.7% top-1 disagreement after 200 steps with nearly equal validation loss; perturbing Adam moments has similar effects (also in OLMo-1B). A targeted stabilization cuts disagreement to 0.83% at a 0.11-nat loss cost.

title: What Makes Recurrence Generalize Across Lengths?
summary: Controlled state-tracking study of recurrent (weight-shared) transformers: atomic operation tokens extrapolate far better than multi-token templates, absolute positions hurt, and scaling the recurrent operator gives 35.1% exact match on 20-40 operations after training on 2-10, where larger fixed-depth transformers get 0%.

title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
summary: With an auxiliary loss, transformers solve multi-step tasks fully latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported. Models trained to pursue a hidden objective (loan decisions, planting a code vulnerability) write CoTs with no trace of it, and activation patching shows the latent computation finishes before the CoT is generated.

title: Character Information in Language Models: A Prompt-Independent Word Store and a Late, Question-Driven Signal That Grows With Scale
summary: Across 16 models (0.6B-14B), first/last/most-frequent letter of a word is linearly decodable from the word's own tokens with no question asked, ~70% already in the token embedding. Asking the question adds a second, late-layer signal at the answer position whose size grows with scale; controls remove length/repetition shortcuts.

title: From Learning Rates to Rotational Schedules: Finite-Horizon Theory on the Sphere
summary: Rewrites learning-rate schedules as rotational schedules for scale-invariant (normalized) parameters. In a geodesically convex spherical setting, a last-iterate bound separates the schedule's scale from its time profile; the optimal schedule tends to linear decay. Predictions about WSD vs linear decay for Adam/Muon vs their hyperball variants hold in LLM pretraining, and give a new schedule that beats cosine and WSD.

title: How Multi-Timescale Memory Cools Optimization: Theory and Evidence from AdEMAMix
summary: Explains AdEMAMix's gain over AdamW through norm dynamics under decoupled weight decay: a slow momentum barely changes the instantaneous update but inflates parameter norms, slowing rotation and acting as an endogenous annealing schedule; controlled interventions in LM pretraining support this.

title: SGD Selects Initialization-Dependent Representation in Overparameterized ReLU Networks
summary: Two-layer bias-free ReLU nets of width m ≥ 4 learning a linear teacher under Gaussian inputs have infinitely many non-aligned exact fits, yet batch-size-one SGD from small init provably drives every neuron to one of the two teacher directions and reaches arbitrarily small error in finite time, with an init-dependent allocation across neurons.

title: Learning the Projection onto the Data Support: Distribution Learning that Avoids Memorization
summary: Learns distributions on (unions of) manifolds by estimating the nearest-point projection onto the data support via an objective whose minimizer is that projection; it adapts to intrinsic dimension, has finite-sample Wasserstein bounds, and, unlike diffusion objectives, cannot be minimized by memorizing training samples.

title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
summary: Estimating the probability of an event chosen after seeing the data, with no fresh samples: Õ(√d) samples suffice for constant MSE on a domain of size d when the selection rule is known, matching the lower bound up to logs and resolving an open question of Feldman et al. Uses sample amplification plus online-learning distribution estimation; a smoothed variant needs only O(log d).

title: Deterministic Proper Positive-Only Learning Is Independent of ZFC
summary: Deterministic proper PAC learnability from positive-only samples is independent of ZFC: a VC-dimension-2 class exists whose deterministic proper learnability is undecidable although a randomized learner learns it, and no finite-character dimension characterizes it. Below a cardinality threshold (including countable domains) a combinatorial characterization holds; under GCH the threshold is sharp.

title: The Value of Labels in Data Selection for Least Squares
summary: Choosing n rows of a dataset (rows of leverage ≤ κ) to fit unweighted OLS: a label-blind selector has optimal worst-case excess ratio dκ/n, while one that sees labels gets between dκ/(2n) and dκΛ_d/n, so labels are worth exactly a factor 2 for d ≤ 4; for grouped designs the constant is 27d/128, and a high-dimensional construction shows labels are worth at most ~√e there.

title: Tight Mistake-Abstention Tradeoffs for Sequential Prediction under Adversarial Injections
summary: Sequential prediction with adversarially injected instances and free abstention on injected points: a weighted-shattering potential gives the conjectured O(d log T) mistakes for known μ, and tight-in-T-and-d mistake/abstention tradeoffs (balanced rate O(√(dT))) for unknown μ and oblivious adversaries.

title: Tight Bounds for Rank Estimation in Turnstile Streams
summary: Determines the space complexity of rank (quantile) estimation in turnstile streams up to a constant: a new lower bound Ω(min{ε^{-1}L^{3/2}log(…), ε^{-2}log U log n, …}) bits that matches Dyadic CountSketch in its regime, with refined algorithms for the remaining regimes.

title: The abc index: Exact Retrieval for Learned Sparse Representations
summary: abc, an exact index for learned sparse retrieval built from standard parts (TAAT, Block-Max MaxScore, binary packing, doc-id reordering). On MS MARCO with four LSR models it is the fastest exact index (6.5-84x Qdrant, 2.9-18x BMP) and, while approximate indexes (Seismic, HNSW) are up to 4.3x faster at k=10, it overtakes them by up to 7.4x at k=1000 with 1.5-3.6x less space.

title: Look Before You Leap: Re-Architecting Disk-Resident Vector Search with TriVS
summary: TriVS for disk-resident ANN: route coarsely with in-memory clusters (no approach-phase I/O), distill routed clusters to a shortlist with compact quantized vectors in memory, then converge with vector-level disk reads. 3.42x PipeANN throughput at Recall@10 = 0.9 with less memory and 64% less I/O.

title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
summary: Zarc: exact k-NN (Euclidean, cosine, inner product, filtered, with updates) over a billion vectors on 4 H100s, keeping only the short rows of half-precision pruning proofs on GPU and fetching remaining candidates from host memory; 10k exact queries in 1.1 s vs 5 min, and 2.2-13.1x faster exact top-10 attention-key retrieval.

title: SJG: A Skyline Joint Graph for Multi-Component Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
summary: Skyline Joint Graph for ANN under query-weighted multi-component distances: since dominance among candidates is weight-independent, each node keeps the skyline of candidates pooled across components; up to 27.9x throughput at 90% Recall@10 and much faster construction.

title: PROSPER: LLMs as Sparse Retrievers for First-Stage Product Search
summary: PROSPER uses LLMs as learned sparse retrievers for first-stage product search, with a literal residual network that re-weights under-weighted literal terms (brands, model ids) and a top-k lexical focusing window for early sparsification; offline gains and online A/B revenue gains.

title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering
summary: RenderEmbed renders text, image and composed inputs into one visual substrate before encoding with a VLM, with anchor tokens for compact embeddings; beats same-size SOTA on MMEB and ViDoRe v2 (+1.7 P@1 over MetaEmbed).

title: Ask Again: Answer-List Instability in Generative Engines
summary: Over 60,000 responses, generative search engines name a different first item 32% of the time for the same prompt; a close leader is identified only 60% of the time after 25 runs. Visibility metrics should report per-item appearance and first-position frequencies with uncertainty.

title: Make Position Uninformative: Exchangeable Self-Distillation Flattens the Lost-in-the-Middle Curve
summary: Shows that with a uniform answer slot and shuffled distractors the optimal reader ignores position, and trains an adapter (ExSD) on shuffled contexts to match the model's answer given the gold document alone; flattens the lost-in-the-middle curve on 1.5B-32B models without gold answers.

title: S$^2$LMR: Supervised Sequential Long-Context Multi-Step Retriever
summary: S²LMR, a supervised sequential multi-step retriever over long contexts (4K-10M tokens) that fixes three train/inference mismatches (easy negatives, noisy prefixes, position-agnostic scoring); matches costlier methods with ~2 GPU-hours of training.

title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
summary: Training recursive LM harnesses with RL gives compositional generalization: training on short tasks transfers to 2-64x longer ones; RLM-27B improves long-context suites by 26.9% with ~2x fewer tokens.

title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models
summary: A carried 'temporal residual' stream (2,752 extra parameters) retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base raises AIME/AMC scores and lets the model reason in hidden state (no-CoT GSM8K 21% → 40%).

title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization
summary: 4,076 audited NL-vs-Lean discrepancies from 832 research-level Lean projects; training on them improves writing Lean inside real projects (NeurIPS'26 Math-AI workshop).

title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study
summary: A frontier model's self-assessed success probability on 87 open geometric-analysis conjectures averaged 0.62 vs 0.10 observed: badly overconfident but still rank-informative (AUROC 0.71).

title: VADE: A Verifiable Agent Data Engine from Professional Sources
summary: VADE builds verifiable analysis tasks for agents in law/finance from public professional sources, exploiting that answers are hard to find but easy to verify.

title: A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming
summary: A matrix analogue of the Lee-Sidford barrier with self-concordance Õ(m), giving the fastest known SDP solver for m ≤ n.
